A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same activation-communication research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original coordination-game and reasoning-benchmark experiments, quantitative ablations in Appendix B, and qualitative examples in Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds results involving Qwen and Gemma models and an activation-space similarity analysis.

M1.justification: The activation-grafting procedure, sum/mean/replacement functions, unequal-dimension handling, and optional MSE-trained mapping matrix remain unchanged. The chain-of-thought and identical-model adaptations already appear in v1's appendix; evaluating additional model families introduces no new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions use Countries, Tip Sheets, Biographies, GSM8k, MMLU, and C4, including the full MMLU results and GSM8k training-data experiment. The added experiments reuse existing data and tasks; Qwen and Gemma change model configurations rather than dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: New Table 4 adds Qwen-2.5-1.5B/3B and Gemma-2-2B/9B as directly evaluated standalone comparators, alongside NLD for the added model pairs. The comparison strategies remain single-model inference and NLD. CIPHER remains unevaluated in both versions.

E3.justification: Table 4 substantially extends evaluation configurations beyond LLaMA to Qwen, Gemma, and mixed-family pairs, explicitly without training the mapping matrix. Appendix B.4 adds a six-pair protocol comparing activation similarity on 3072 C4 sentences with Biographies gains over average individual performance. Existing experiments retain their stated settings.

E4.justification: v2 adds targeted model-family robustness checks and Appendix B.4/Figure 11, investigating whether activation-space similarity tracks communication gains. The earlier layer-selection, token-modification, chain-of-thought, mapping-data, identical-model, and debate-round analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same 95% bootstrap intervals with 1000 iterations in Table 2 and retain the existing plus/minus uncertainty entries. New Table 4 continues that reporting style without new run-count, seed, or uncertainty-method information. The similarity plot adds no correlation significance test or uncertainty estimate.

E6.justification: Table 4 adds substantial results for five additional model pairs. For Qwen-2.5-1.5B/3B, AC scores 89.6/70.0 on Biographies/GSM8k versus NLD's 63.2/65.0. Gains are not universal: Gemma-pair AC scores 88.1 on Biographies versus the individual 9B model's 94.6. Figure 11 adds a positive similarity–gain trend. Previously reported table values and qualitative examples remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix B.4 introduces an explicit activation-space similarity definition, ||Y^T X||_F^2 / (||X||_F^2 ||Y||_F^2), for the new analysis. The original method mathematics, assumptions, and FLOP derivations are unchanged; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same core claims: activation-based communication, no additional task-specific parameters or data, and up to 27.0% improvement with less than one-quarter the compute. New experiments support the existing contribution rather than redefine it.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations for communication across model families through limited last-token perturbation or shared representations, and interprets greater activation similarity as making grafted information more useful. It also invokes the platonic representation hypothesis. The original alignment, internal-access, and interpretability limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 documents that the added model-family experiments omit the mapping matrix and explains how the similarity analysis constructs activation matrices using the same 3072 C4 sentences previously used to train W. Existing training hyperparameters and resource-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds connections to latent reasoning through Geiping et al. and Hao et al., and to shared representations through Huh et al., Moschella et al., and Kornblith et al. It also expands the CIPHER exclusion rationale to mention a shared embedding table. Existing research positioning is otherwise retained.

P1.justification: Changes comprise localized discussion additions, a new appendix subsection, impact and acknowledgement statements, and heading/front-matter edits. Most prose and the overall section sequence remain unchanged; the document is not extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from a single-column layout to an ICML two-column format, extensively reflowing equations, tables, and figure placement and sizing. Table 4 and Figure 11 are new. Existing Figures 1–10 retain identical artwork, while appendix tables are renumbered and reformatted.

improvement.justification: The added model-family results and alignment analysis provide a modest empirical improvement over v1's LLaMA-only validation. Benefits are tempered by overinterpretation: Section 4.2 says AC beats NLD 'across the board', although Table 4 includes a 64-versus-75 GSM8k loss and a 75–75 tie, and calls the findings 'proof' of the platonic representation hypothesis. The broader evidence is useful, but supports narrower conclusions.
